text:
incident-bot: PAGER — Private VPC (Peregrine Systems) egress errors detected. 95th-percentile outbound failures to customer NLB target group. Severity: P2. Impact: degraded API traffic to customer tenant on Dedicated pool. Auto-alert created and oncall paged.

amanda: acked. oncall here — starting investigation. is this across all AZs? any changes pushed in the last 30m?

lee: I'm seeing increased TCP RSTs from the NLB fronting Peregrine. Flow logs show a spike in REJECT from SGs around 12:02 UTC. No infra deploys in last 40m according to deploy-bot.

rafael: I've opened a line to SE to confirm customer traffic patterns. They're seeing 502s and timeouts from our edge -> customer NLB. Customer says they haven't changed anything.

priya: quick hypothesis: healthchecks failing and NLB cycling targets causing connection churn + DNS failover oddities. Could also be conntrack exhaustion on the NAT gateway in the tenant's private subnet.

amanda: steps — 1) confirm security group deltas 2) check NLB target health and backend status 3) verify DNS TTL/weighting in case of failover 4) if conntrack, throttle/shorten sessions or rotate NAT.

lee: running checks now. output:
```
# nlb target health
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/tg-ps-1
# shows many targets Unhealthy (code: 503)
# vpc flow logs snippet
12:02:11 ACCEPT tcp 10.0.5.12:443 -> 10.1.8.45:52345
12:02:13 REJECT tcp 10.0.5.12:443 -> 10.1.8.45:52346 SG-REJECT rule id 200
```

rafael: customer reports their ALB health checks are green on their side. This suggests something on our egress path or SGs blocking specific ephemeral ports.

amanda: @lee please check our egress security group rules for the VPC endpoint/ENI that handles tenant outbound. Any recent automated config changes?

lee: checked audit logs — no manual SG edits. However, a policy automation run 35m ago applied a tightened SG for the dedicated pool to block 1024-65535 from certain subnets (intended for other tenants). Looks like rule scoping mis-flagged Peregrine's ENIs.

priya: that explains sg-reject. mitigation options:
- rollback the automation (fast)
- add explicit allow for Peregrine's ENIs on ephemeral range (fastest)
- temporarily route Peregrine through a secondary egress in another AZ (safer but takes longer)

amanda: prioritize low-blast fastest fix: add explicit allow for Peregrine ENIs. @lee can you patch SG and run smoke? Also update incident timeline.

lee: applying rule now
```
# add SG rule to allow ephemeral range for tenant ENIs
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abcd1234 --protocol tcp --port 1024-65535 --cidr 10.1.8.45/32 --description "temp allow for Peregrine tenant egress"
```

lee: rule added. re-checking target health... targets return to Healthy in ~40s. Observed 200s on retried requests.

rafael: customer confirms traffic recovered, API errors dropping to baseline. they're asking for root cause and ETA for permanent fix.

amanda: good. immediate mitigation worked. Next: 1) document rollback window 2) schedule permanent SG scoping fix to avoid misclassification of tenant ENIs 3) verify DNS weights weren't shifted during the incident.

priya: I will open a PR to update automation scoping and add a safeguard unit test in policy-run pipeline to detect overlapping ENI sets. ETA for PR + rollout: 4h.

lee: also investigating conntrack counters — NAT gateway looked healthy; no exhaustion. We'll keep monitoring for 30m.

amanda: prepare customer-facing summary and postmortem stub. @rafael can you send initial note? Keep wording: mitigated, brief cause (automation SG tighten), next steps, and offer follow-up call.

rafael: sending initial note to Peregrine now. Draft: "We observed outbound failures to your NLB caused by an overly-broad security group update in our dedicated pool automation that mistakenly matched your ENIs. We applied a temporary allow rule to restore traffic and are implementing a scoped fix. We will follow up with a full RCA and timeline."

incident-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" at 3642001300. Pager silence scheduled for 30m.

amanda: handing off to @evan for 30m monitoring window and the post-incident task list. evan, please collect logs for the postmortem: flow logs, SG audit diff, policy-run diff, NLB target health history, customer support thread.

evan: taking handoff. I have the checklist. Will consolidate artifacts and start a postmortem draft. Anything urgent?

amanda: none for now. note: keep the temporary SG allow in place until PR is live and validated (target: 4h). After that, schedule a controlled rollback during low traffic.

lee: I'll keep collecting flow logs and set an alert on SG-reject spikes for that dedicated pool.

priya: also adding a unit-test to policy pipeline to compare ENI tag sets against target exclusion lists to prevent future mis-scope.

rafael: customer thanks the team. asking for regular updates; I'll coordinate.

evan: logging final timeline and artifacts. closing this thread once postmortem stub is created. :white_check_mark:
